MOBILE APP · MOTION PREVIEW
01 / The project

A small pause in a busy day.

What if ordering your favorite matcha could feel just as considered as visiting the café itself?

More than just
ordering matcha.
Yume Mori is a conceptual mobile ordering experience designed around a simple idea: make everyday café visits feel effortless without losing the charm of the place itself. The app connects menu discovery, thoughtful customization, weekend availability, and scheduled pickup.
Project typeIndependent UX/UI concept
RoleUX Research framing · UI Design
Deliverables4 key screens · Design system
ToolsFigma · Prototyping
02 / The opportunity

A lovely café.
A little friction.

The design starts with a few practical observations and turns them into questions worth exploring.

Starting observations

Simple needs, real moments.

Long queues can interrupt a café visit. A clear menu makes browsing easier, while weekend-only items create questions about availability. The project brief also identified the absence of first-party online ordering.

Design hypotheses

Clarity creates calm.

Showing availability early, keeping customization options easy to scan, and clarifying the pickup plan may make the experience feel more predictable. These are design assumptions, not validated research findings.

How might we…

Make ordering ahead feel as thoughtful and welcoming as the café experience itself?

03 / Experience strategy

One easy flow.
Four little moments.

The experience keeps the decision-making journey familiar, with the most relevant information visible when guests need it.

01

Discover

Welcome customers with a clear entry point and a glimpse of weekend specials.

02

Browse

Explore drinks and treats with simple categories and visible availability.

03

Customize

Choose matcha, milk, sweetness, and ice without overwhelming the screen.

04

Review

Confirm items, pricing, and pickup details in one clear summary.

04 / Final interface

Designed for
the little details.

Four connected high-fidelity screens using a quiet palette, readable controls, and a consistent visual rhythm.

01 — Home

An inviting first impression with direct paths to ordering and seasonal highlights.

02 — Menu

Menu categories and product cards make favorites easy to discover.

03 — Customize

Step-by-step choices preserve flexibility without adding visual clutter.

04 — Checkout

A legible summary brings together fulfillment, items, and estimated total.

05 / Visual identity

Soft colors.
Clear intentions.

The visual system draws from matcha, natural textures, and the café’s gentle atmosphere.

07 / Reflection

A little more room for
the things that matter.

The concept explores how a practical task can carry a café’s personality into a digital setting. Next steps would include testing the ordering flow with customers and validating menu data, pickup capacity, and fulfillment options with café staff.
